3.7 Division Algorithm for Polynomials
You know that a cubic polynomial has at most three zeroes. However, if you are given
only one zero, can you find the other two?  For example, let us consider the cubic polynomial
x3 + 3x2 – x – 3. If  one of its zeroes is 1, then you know that this polynomial is divisible by
x – 1. Therefore, we would get the quotient x2 – 2x – 3 on dividing by x – 1.
We get the factors of x2 – 2x – 3 by splitting the middle term. The factors are (x + 1) and
(x – 3). This gives us
x3 – 3x2 – x + 3 = (x – 1) (x2 – 2x – 3)
= (x – 1) (x + 1) (x – 3)
So, the three zeroes of the cubic polynomial are 1, – 1, 3.
